basis: Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the syndrome; ocular and skeletal abnormalities occur in only 1/5 each.
Microcephaly defines the syndrome; dilated cardiomyopathy occurs in 4/9. Recurrent infections do not establish intrinsic immunodeficiency.
Eye, hearing and skeletal disease define it; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%, cleft palate in 30-79%. Ectodermal skin/hair dysfunction omitted by cap.
Neurodevelopmental and progressive neurologic disease span the umbrella; hepatic, glycosylation and immune abnormalities are subtype-dependent.
Psychiatric dysphoria; no defining damage to an organ axis.
Benign neoplasm arising in breast or rarely prostate; both sites lie outside the axes.
Spirillum minus infection; systemic fever and transient rash do not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited skin and hair pigment disorder; reported nystagmus and photophobia lack frequencies or documented visual loss supporting ocular involvement.
Cutaneous vascular lesion composed of abnormal endothelial-lined channels.
Severe intellectual disability and microcephaly define the syndrome together with strabismus, reported in 80-99%.
Hormone-secreting neoplasm of the pituitary gland; no other organ injury is established across the group.
Intellectual disability and seizures define it; cataract/glaucoma occurs in 3/6 and cleft palate in 2/6. Small hands and feet alone do not establish locomotor dysfunction.
Immune-mediated muscle spasms, skeletal disease and alopecia define it; malabsorption/diarrhea is a major feature (~50%+). Reported renal/endocrine findings omitted by cap.
Congenital secretory enteropathy; hepatic steatosis with elevated transaminases occurs in 5/5. Hypoglycemia may reflect impaired nutrition rather than intrinsic endocrine disease.
Congenital ectopic pancreatic tissue; no endocrine dysfunction or damage to the sites containing the tissue is established.
Anxiety disorder with panic attacks and agoraphobia; no defining organ damage.
Hypocellular marrow failure with multilineage cytopenias; hypogonadism and elevated FSH occur in 2/2, with pituitary hypoplasia in 1/2.
Glycogen branching enzyme deficiency with childhood myopathy; cardiac, hepatic and peripheral nerve involvement are not established at >=30% for this form.
Parasitic infection directly affecting skeletal muscle.
Acute infection and inflammation of the external ear.
Inherited hair-shaft disorder with alopecia and follicular hyperkeratosis.
Acute infectious inflammation of the frontal sinus; sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
NFKB2 immunodeficiency; central adrenal insufficiency in 4/4 and alopecia/nail dystrophy in 2/4. Recurrent respiratory infections and asthma are separately diagnosed conditions.
KY-related disease encompasses skeletal myopathy and neurologic disease, including hereditary spastic paraplegia.
Infection produces toxin that blocks neuromuscular transmission; respiratory failure, diplopia and dysphagia reflect neural blockade rather than separate organ damage.
